title: Ash brown balayage: who it suits and how to keep it cool
seoTitle: Ash Brown Balayage: Who It Suits, How to Keep It | Emrahair
description: Ash brown balayage: what it is, which skin undertones it suits, why ash tones turn brassy and how blue or purple shampoo and a salon gloss keep it cool.
lede: Ash brown balayage places cool, light brown highlights with a soft gray and beige cast over a brown base. It suits cool and neutral skin undertones best, it is reached on dark hair by lifting and toning correctly, and it needs regular toning at home and in the salon to stay cool.

sections.heading: What is ash brown balayage?
body: Light to medium brown is what Turkish salons call kumral, and “ash” (küllü) means the warm red and gold reflections in that brown have been neutralized and pulled toward a cool, slightly gray and beige undertone. So ash brown is neither gray nor blonde: it is a soft, matte brown that does not turn orange, even in sunlight.

As a balayage, the shade is not applied all over. Your roots stay close to your natural brown, and ash brown light is swept onto selected strands from mid-length to the ends. The result looks deeper and more natural than single-process color and grows out without a harsh line. Done with the Air Touch technique, the blend is softer still.

sections.heading: Who does ash brown suit? Know your skin undertone
body: With ash shades, what matters is not how light or dark your skin is but its undertone. Two complexions of the same depth, one reflecting pink and blue, the other gold and peach, will wear the same hair color very differently.

On cool and neutral undertones, ash brown makes skin look clear and calms redness. On warm undertones, a fully ash color can wash the face out; a beige or neutral brown, or ash highlights kept toward the ends and away from the face, usually looks more balanced. Every color service at Emrahair starts with a consultation, where your undertone is assessed with you. To get an idea at home, try these:
list: If the veins on your inner wrist look blue or purple, your undertone is most likely cool
If they look greenish, you may be warm; somewhere in between usually means neutral
If silver jewelry brightens your face, cool is likely; if gold does, warm is likely
If you burn easily in the sun you may lean cool; if you tan easily you may lean warm

sections.heading: How ash brown works on dark Turkish hair
body: Dark brown and near-black hair naturally carries a warm underlying pigment. As the hair lifts, that pigment shows: first red, then orange, and yellow at lighter levels. Ash brown is created by toning out that warmth. On the color wheel, blue sits opposite orange and purple sits opposite yellow, which is why those two are the basis of every ash tone.

The key is lifting the hair to the right level before toning. Putting an ash toner over a strand that has not lifted enough and is still orange often gives a muddy, greenish or quickly reddening result. On uncolored dark hair the process is usually more predictable; on hair that has had dark dye before, lightening may be split over several sessions. If you are moving away from previous color, see our [hair color and color change](/sac-boyama) options as well.

sections.heading: Why do ash tones turn brassy?
body: The most common complaint with ash brown balayage is that a few weeks in, the color warms up and drifts toward red or yellow. The reason is simple: the toner pigments that create the cool tone sit close to the surface of the hair and wash out a little with every shampoo. The lightened hair underneath is warm, so as the toner fades, that warmth comes back through.
In other words, brassiness is not a mistake; it is how ash tones behave. The right care slows it down, and it is easy to refresh. The main things that speed it up:
list: Washing very often, and with hot water
Sun, sea water and pool water
Hard water and strong, sulfate-based shampoos
Blow-dryers, curling irons and flat irons used without heat protectant

sections.heading: At home: blue shampoo or purple shampoo?
body: The basics of color care are a sulfate-free shampoo made for colored hair, lukewarm water and a heat protectant before any hot tools. Skipping the wash for the first two days after coloring also helps the color last. For ash tones, you add a toning shampoo on top of that.

Blue shampoo neutralizes orange and copper warmth, which is what ash brown and dark brown balayage mostly need. Purple shampoo neutralizes yellow, so it suits any ends that have been lifted to beige or ash blonde. For most hair, once a week with a short leave-in time is enough. Using a toning shampoo too often, or leaving it on too long, can make hair look dull or darker than it is.

sections.heading: In the salon: a gloss or hair glaze refresh
body: Home care slows fading, but toner eventually washes out completely. At that point there is no need to redo the balayage; the ash tone can be refreshed in the salon with a toner or gloss. Emrahair offers a Gloss Service (Parlatma Servisi) at [[474011-1]] and a Hair Glaze (Saç Cilası) at [[237974-1]]. Both revive the color on colored hair and add shine, and you will find them with the other treatments on our [keratin and hair care page](/keratin).

Because the roots stay close to your natural color, the balayage itself is usually refreshed every 3 to 6 months; a gloss in between, once the tone starts to fade, brings the color back toward its first-day coolness. For the techniques and how the appointment works, see our [balayage and Air Touch page](/balyaj).

faq.q: Who does ash brown hair suit?
faq.a: Ash brown suits cool and neutral skin undertones best: on people whose wrist veins look blue or purple and whom silver jewelry flatters, it makes the skin look clear. On warm undertones, a fully ash shade can wash the face out. In that case, a beige or neutral brown, or ash highlights only at the ends, is more balanced.

faq.q: Why does ash brown balayage turn brassy?
faq.a: The toner pigments that create the cool tone sit close to the surface of the hair and wash out a little with every shampoo. The lightened hair underneath is naturally warm, so yellow, orange or red reflections show through over time. Hot water, sun, hard water and styling without heat protectant speed this up.

faq.q: Should I use purple or blue shampoo on ash brown hair?
faq.a: Blue shampoo neutralizes the orange warmth in brown shades, so it is usually the better choice for ash brown balayage. Purple shampoo neutralizes yellow, which makes it better for ends that have been lifted to beige or blonde. For most hair, once a week with a short leave-in time is enough.

faq.q: Can you get ash brown balayage on black hair?
faq.a: Yes, but dark hair has to be lifted enough first. Black hair passes through red and orange as it lightens, and ash brown is created by toning out that warmth. On hair that has had dark dye before, lightening may be split over several sessions.
